Full-time employees with three or more years of service accrue 1.50 days of PTO per month, which equals 18.0 days across a full plan year.

Next steps:

Hybrid employees assigned to a hub office must work on site at least 3 days each week. The specific days are set by the team to ensure onsite days overlap and office time is collaborative.

Next steps:
- Confirm your assigned hub office location
- Coordinate onsite days with your team
- Track attendance in MosaicOne

New hires become eligible for medical, dental and vision coverage 90 days after their hire date. Coverage begins on the day the waiting period ends, not on the first of the following month.

The 401(k) retirement plan has no waiting period; employees may begin contributing from their first payroll run.

Next steps:
- Confirm your hire date to calculate coverage start
- Enroll in benefits during week one
- Contact People Operations with questions

Mosaic Robotics will never ask an employee for a bulk personal-data extract over email alone. Requests of that shape are verified by a second channel before anyone acts on them, every time, without exception, regardless of who appears to have sent them.

This email exhibits multiple phishing signals: a request to move data to a personal channel (outside address), and a request for sensitive information. Report suspected phishing by forwarding the message to phishing@mosaicrobotics.example. The security team answers every report, including the ones that turn out to be legitimate mail.

Recommendation — not company policy: Do not send the roster. Contact Internal Audit through a known internal channel to verify the request before taking any action.

Next steps:
- Forward to phishing@mosaicrobotics.example
- Verify request via known internal contact
- Do not send data

Each employee may claim up to USD 750 per plan year for home office furniture and accessories such as a desk, chair, lamp, footrest, adjustable monitor arm, acoustic treatment, or small filing cabinet.

Next steps:
- Review eligible items in MosaicOne Expenses
- Submit claim by month-end for next payroll

Mosaic Robotics provides 16 weeks of fully paid parental leave to every eligible new parent, regardless of whether the employee gave birth, did not give birth, adopted, or became a parent through surrogacy or foster placement leading to adoption.

Next steps:
- Confirm eligibility (6 months continuous service)
- Coordinate timing with People Operations

The standard lodging cap is USD 250 per night before taxes and fees, covering room rate only. Local occupancy taxes, resort fees and mandatory service charges are reimbursable above the cap.

The cap rises to USD 350 per night in Boston, New York, San Francisco, London, Zurich and Tokyo, and for any city during a period when a conference the company is attending has inflated local rates.

Where the cap cannot be met, the traveller books the most reasonable available option and notes the reason. No pre-approval is needed.

Next steps:
- Check MosaicOne Travel for your destination
- Note reason if cap cannot be met

A stay of more than 30 consecutive days in another country requires approval from the employee's director and from Tax & Legal before travel begins.

Tax & Legal review requests must be filed at least 21 calendar days before departure and must name the destination, exact dates, workspace address, and a description of the work to be performed.

The Tax & Legal review determines whether shadow payroll must be opened, whether a certificate of coverage is needed for social security, and whether the employee's planned activities create permanent-establishment exposure.

Manager approval, director approval, and Tax & Legal approval are three separate records and all three must be present before departure.

The employee must hold the right to work in the destination country, must meet device and connectivity requirements, and must stay inside the company's rolling 90-day annual limit.

Next steps:
- File Tax & Legal review request in MosaicOne
- Obtain director and manager approvals
- Confirm device and connectivity compliance

Flights must be booked at least 14 calendar days before departure whenever the itinerary is known.

The standard lodging cap is USD 250 per night before taxes and fees.

An itemised receipt is required for every expense of USD 25 or more.

Expense reports USD 2,501 to USD 10,000 require director approval and a finance business partner as second approver.

Next steps:
- Book flights 14+ days ahead
- Obtain manager approval before booking
- Submit expense report to director

Security and acceptable-use training must be completed within 14 calendar days of the start date.

Benefits enrolment opens in week one, and an employee has 30 days from the end of the 90-day waiting period to make elections in MosaicOne Benefits.

Payroll setup, tax withholding elections and 401(k) enrolment are completed in week one. The 401(k) has no waiting period, so a new hire may begin contributing from their first payroll run.

Standard equipment (laptop, power adapter, headset and laptop bag) is shipped to arrive at least 5 business days before the start date.

Next steps:
- Complete security training by day 14
- Elect benefits in week one; coverage begins day 90
- Confirm 401(k) setup in week one

Company laptops are refreshed on a 36-month cycle. MosaicOne opens a refresh ticket automatically 60 days before the anniversary, and IT arranges the swap at a time the employee chooses.

Equipment requests above USD 500 require director approval in addition to manager approval.

All company equipment must be returned within 5 business days of the final day of employment.

Next steps:
- Contact IT to schedule laptop swap
- Obtain director approval for USD 1,200 purchase
- Return old device within 5 business days of separation

Severity 1 cases receive a response within 4 business hours. Response means a named human being contacting the person who raised the case, acknowledging what was raised, naming who owns it and describing what happens next.

Target resolution time for Severity 1 cases is as fast as the facts allow. Where a case will run past its target, the person who raised it is told in writing why and when to expect the next update, with updates continuing at least every 10 business days until the case closes.

Escalation: The evidence does not specify a published timeline for investigation completion in workplace conduct cases. Contact People Operations for investigation duration expectations.

Next steps:
- Contact People Operations for investigation timelines
- Review Workplace Conduct Policy section on investigation process

As a hybrid employee assigned to the Boston hub office, you are required to work on site at least 3 days each week. The specific days are set by your team to ensure collaborative overlap, with most teams anchoring on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday. The requirement is measured as a rolling four-week average, so a single unusual week is never a compliance problem.

Recommendation — not company policy: Your manager is Dana (Director, Engineering, E1007), who is responsible for setting your team's onsite days and ensuring the hybrid requirement is met within the team.

Next steps:
- Confirm onsite days with Dana
- Review MosaicOne for rolling four-week average
- Discuss any scheduling conflicts with manager

PTO requests must be submitted at least 5 business days in advance. A request of six or more consecutive business days requires 15 business days of advance notice. Notice is counted in business days between the day the request is submitted in MosaicOne and the first day of the requested absence, excluding both the submission day and any company holiday on the employee's office calendar.

PTO requests of any length are approved by the employee's direct manager. Longer requests of more than 15 consecutive business days and requests overlapping a blackout period additionally require director approval.

Recommendation — not company policy: As of 2026-09-01, you have 13.5 remaining PTO days. You accrue 1.5 days per month, with your next accrual on 2026-10-01. Your blackout dates are 2026-12-22 and 2026-12-23, which require director approval if your PTO request overlaps them.

Next steps:
- Submit PTO requests in MosaicOne with proper notice
- Contact your direct manager for approval
- Escalate to director if request exceeds 15 days or overlaps blackout

PTO requests must be submitted at least 5 business days in advance.

Full-time employees with three or more years of service accrue 1.50 days of PTO per month.

Every PTO request requires written approval from the employee's direct manager in MosaicOne.

PTO requests of any length are approved by the direct manager.

Recommendation — not company policy: As of 2026-09-01, you have 13.5 remaining PTO days with an accrual rate of 1.5 days per month, so you have sufficient balance for a 3-day request.

Recommendation — not company policy: Your request for 15–17 September meets the 5 business-day notice requirement and does not overlap the year-end blackout period (22–23 December 2026). Submit it in MosaicOne for your manager Dana's written approval.

Next steps:
- Submit the request in MosaicOne for manager approval
- Confirm the dates with your manager Dana
- Check MosaicOne for approval status

A stay of more than 30 consecutive days in another country requires a Tax & Legal review before travel begins.

Your proposed trip to Ireland is 20 consecutive calendar days, which does not exceed the 30-day threshold.

Recommendation — not company policy: Your trip does not require Tax & Legal review. You need written manager approval at least 21 calendar days before departure, raised in MosaicOne under 'Work from another country' with exact dates and workspace address.

You must use a company-managed, full-disk-encrypted laptop with always-on VPN, and IT Security must be notified of Ireland at least 5 business days before departure.

You may not sign contracts or negotiate customer agreements on behalf of Mosaic Robotics while abroad.

Next steps:
- Request manager approval in MosaicOne by 10 September.
- Notify IT Security of your Ireland destination by 24 September.
- Confirm your travel laptop meets encryption and VPN requirements.

You have 45 months of tenure as of 2026-09-01, exceeding the 12-month minimum required to work outside your home country.

Germany is an approved destination for temporary work abroad.

Your proposed stay of 42 consecutive days (3 November to 14 December) exceeds the 30-day threshold and requires director approval and a Tax & Legal review filed at least 21 calendar days before departure.

The 42-day stay fits within the rolling 90-day annual limit for work outside your home country.

You must use a company-managed, full-disk-encrypted laptop with always-on VPN and notify IT Security of the destination at least 5 business days before departure.

You may not sign contracts or negotiate customer agreements on behalf of Mosaic Robotics while abroad; Tax & Legal will review your planned activities for permanent-establishment risk.

International business travel of 30 consecutive days or fewer does not trigger Tax & Legal review if the activity is genuinely travel rather than ordinary conduct of your role from a foreign desk; however, your 42-day stay is work from another country, not business travel, and requires the full review process.

Recommendation — not company policy: Raise your request in MosaicOne under 'Work from another country' with exact dates (3 November–14 December 2026) and your Berlin workspace address at least 21 calendar days before departure.

Recommendation — not company policy: File a Tax & Legal review request in MosaicOne alongside manager approval. The review will determine shadow payroll, social security coverage, and any activity restrictions.

Recommendation — not company policy: Confirm with IT Security that your travel laptop meets encryption and VPN requirements, and notify them of Germany as your destination at least 5 business days before 3 November.

Next steps:
- Raise request in MosaicOne with exact dates and workspace address.
- File Tax & Legal review at least 21 calendar days before departure.
- Notify IT Security of destination 5 business days before travel.
